nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $n \ne 0$, and write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of a prime $p$ in the prime factorization of $n$. Then $n$ is $k$-full if and only if $k \le v_p(n)$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$.
nodes.title: Factorization criterion for $k$-full numbers

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is $1$-full if and only if $n \ne 0$, since $p^1 = p$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$.
nodes.title: The $1$-full numbers

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is $0$-full if and only if $n \ne 0$, since $p^0 = 1$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$.
nodes.title: The $0$-full numbers

nodes.summary: Let $j \le k$ be natural numbers. Every $k$-full natural number is $j$-full.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of $k$-fullness in $k$

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number. Every $k$-full natural number is $2$-full.
nodes.title: For $k \ge 2$, $k$-full numbers are $2$-full

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $1$ is $k$-full: it is nonzero and has no prime divisors.
nodes.title: One is $k$-full

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is $2$-full if and only if $n \ne 0$ and $p^2$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$. These are the squarefull (also called powerful) numbers.
nodes.title: The $2$-full numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. A natural number $n$ is $k$-full if $n \ne 0$ and $p^k$ divides $n$ for every prime $p$ dividing $n$.
nodes.title: $k$-full numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $0$ is not $k$-full.
nodes.title: Zero is not $k$-full

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, the powerful part of $n$ divides $n$.
nodes.title: The powerful part of $n$ divides $n$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $p$, write $v_p(n)$ for the exponent of $p$ in the prime factorization of $n$ (it is $0$ when $p$ is not a prime factor of $n$). Then the exponent of $p$ in the powerful part of $n$ equals $v_p(n)$ if $v_p(n) \ge 2$, and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Prime exponents of the powerful part

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n \ge 1$ and a prime $p$, let $v_p(n)$ be the exponent of $p$ in $n$. The powerful (or $2$-full) part of $n$ is the product of the prime powers $p^{v_p(n)}$ over the primes $p$ dividing $n$ with $v_p(n) \ge 2$ (and $1$ if there are none). The powerful part of $0$ is defined to be $1$.
nodes.title: Powerful part of a natural number

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
